$comment: The platform's default model, in one place, so that no component decides it
on its own. Every package that needs a model reads this file; nothing
hardcodes a model id, a quantization or a size.
Every field below is a CLAIM, and this repository's rule is that a claim
carries the address it was read from. `citedAs` is that address. `verified`
says whether anything has actually checked the claim against the thing it
describes — and it is false for everything here, because the machine this
was written on cannot reach huggingface.co (the egress proxy answers 403 to
CONNECT) and no local server has been run against it.
`scripts/verify-model.ts` turns the false into a true by asking a running
server what it is serving and comparing. Until it has been run, treat every
size and every capability here as transcribed, not measured.
$effectiveContextComment: The number that matters, and the reason it is small on purpose.
A model that physically supports a million tokens still runs here at 8192,
because ai-storage exists to solve context scarcity rather than to hide it.
If the benchmark were run at the native maximum it would measure the model's
context window and nothing about the storage layer.

engines.$comment: ai-storage depends on neither. See ai-storage/src/model/local-model.ts.

constrained.purpose: testing on a 16 GB machine; explicitly not the quality reference
constrained.targetHardware: MacBook Air M4, 16 GB unified memory

reference.purpose: the canonical ai-storage environment; benchmark results without a profile mean this one
reference.targetHardware: Apple Silicon >= 32 GB, or NVIDIA GPU >= 24 GB VRAM

quality.purpose: measure quantization damage — is a failure the storage layer's or the compression's?
quality.targetHardware: 48-64 GB unified memory, or 48 GB+ VRAM

weights.$comment: Not resolved from this machine — see the note at the top of this file.

$localOnlyComment: When AI_STORAGE_LOCAL_ONLY is true, a base URL that is not a loopback
address is refused at startup rather than at request time, because a
privacy guarantee that fails on the first request is not a guarantee.
